overview: Pencarrow is a Georgian country house on the edge of Bodmin Moor near Wadebridge, still the home of the same family, the Molesworth-St Aubyns, after almost 500 years, and not part of the National Trust. That gives it a lived-in, slightly eccentric charm.

There’s plenty for families: 50 acres of grounds with gardens that change through the seasons, an Iron Age fort, a children’s play area with a little slate-roofed Wendy house, and a café. Dogs are welcome too.

expect.title: Guided house tours
expect.text: Tours reveal hidden passages, portraits whose eyes follow you and statues wearing top hats.

expect.title: Gardens and grounds
expect.text: A Grade II listed garden with something in flower through the seasons, and an Iron Age fort in the grounds.

expect.title: For children
expect.text: A play area with a Wendy house next to the café.

goodToKnow.label: Café
goodToKnow.text: Light lunches, cakes (with gluten-free options) and cream teas, made with Cornish produce.

week.text: A good half day inland when you want a change from the beach, with something for adults and children. It’s close to Wadebridge and the Camel Trail.

pairWith.why: the market town on the Camel Trail
a spooky indoor visit in Bodmin

tips: Join a guided tour to hear the house’s stories.

setting.note: A historic house plus gardens and grounds
